page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7se.4xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at 2.9 GHz. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks place this instance consistently in the average tier for its hardware class. The Intel Xeon processor delivers a single-core stress-ng score of 1866.58 and a multi-core score of 15529.0. Memory bandwidth tests show 845.59 GB/sec for cached small-block reads, dropping to 88.26 GB/sec for large-block uncached reads. In cryptographic and compression workloads, the instance achieves a PassMark CPU encryption score of 14610.14 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 84.09 GB/sec. Notably, the instance demonstrates strong performance in text generation for small language models (135M), reaching 271.33 tokens/sec, while maintaining average speeds of 11.91 tokens/sec for medium (7B) models.

From a resource density perspective, the ecs.g7se.4xlarge offers a balanced cost-to-performance profile for general-purpose workloads. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures predictable performance without the noisy-neighbor risks of shared-core instances. However, the lack of local NVMe SSD storage means that applications requiring high-IOPS local scratch space will face latency tradeoffs by relying entirely on network storage.

This instance is appropriate for balanced enterprise workloads, including medium-scale web serving, database operations, software compilation, and lightweight machine learning inference. Its 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and dedicated Intel Xeon cores make it a stable platform for application servers, CI/CD pipelines, and Redis caching layers.
